sections.text_helper: Section 34.3.11 "PWM mode" in chapter 34 (General-purpose timers (TIM12)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1298.
sections.section_content:
Pulse width modulation mode is used to generate a signal with a frequency determined by
the value of the TIM_ARR register and a duty cycle determined by the value of the
TIM_CCRx register.
The PWM mode can be selected independently on each channel (one PWM per tim_ocx
output) by writing 0110 (PWM mode 1) or 0111 (PWM mode 2) in the OCxM bits in the
TIM_CCMRx register. The corresponding preload register must be enabled by setting the
OCxPE bit in the TIM_CCMRx register, and eventually the autoreload preload register (in
upcounting or center-aligned modes) by setting the ARPE bit in the TIM_CR1 register.
As the preload registers are transferred to the shadow registers only when an update event
occurs, before starting the counter, all registers must be initialized by setting the UG bit in
the TIM_EGR register.
The tim_ocx polarity is software programmable using the CCxP bit in the TIM_CCER
register. It can be programmed as active high or active low. The tim_ocx output is enabled
by the CCxE bit in the TIM_CCER register. Refer to the TIM_CCERx register description for
more details.
In PWM mode (1 or 2), TIM_CNT and TIM_CCRx are always compared to determine
whether TIM_CNT ≤ TIM_CCRx.
The timer is able to generate PWM in edge-aligned mode only since the counter is
upcounting.
In the following example, the user considers PWM mode 1. The reference PWM signal
tim_ocxref is high as long as TIM_CNT < TIM_CCRx else it becomes low. If the compare
value in TIM_CCRx is greater than the autoreload value (in TIM_ARR) then tim_ocxref is
held at 1. If the compare value is 0 then tim_ocxref is held at 0. Figure449 shows some
edge-aligned PWM waveforms in an example where TIM_ARR = 8.
[Figure 449. Edge-aligned PWM waveforms (ARR = 8)]
Dithering mode
The PWM mode effective resolution can be increased by enabling the dithering mode, using
the DITHEN bit in the TIM_CR1 register. This applies to both the CCR (for duty cycle
resolution increase) and ARR (for PWM frequency resolution increase).
The operating principle is to have the actual CCR (or ARR) value slightly changed (adding
or not one timer clock period) over 16 consecutive PWM periods, with predefined patterns.
This allows a 16-fold resolution increase, considering the average duty cycle or PWM
period. Figure450 presents the dithering principle applied to four consecutive PWM cycles.
[Figure 450. Dithering principle]
When the dithering mode is enabled, the register coding is changed as follows (see
Figure451 for example):
• The four LSBs are coding for the enhanced resolution part (fractional part).
• The MSBs are left-shifted to the bits 19:4 and are coding for the base value.
Note: The following sequence must be followed when resetting the DITHEN bit:
1. CEN and ARPE bits must be reset
2. The DITHEN bit must be reset
3. The CCIF flags must be cleared
4. The CEN bit can be set (eventually with ARPE = 1).
[Figure 451. Data format and register coding in dithering mode]

Note: The maximum TIM_ARR and TIM_CCRy values are limited to 0xFFFEF in dithering mode
(corresponds to 65534 for the integer part and 15 for the dithered part).
As shown on Figure452, the dithering mode is used to increase the PWM resolution
whatever the PWM frequency.
[Figure 452. PWM resolution vs frequency]
The duty cycle and/or period changes are spread over 16 consecutive periods, as described
in Figure453.

described in Table339. The dithering sequence is done to have increments distributed as
